papers.title: Microfluidic Bioprinting of Heterogeneous 3D Tissue Constructs Using Low‐Viscosity Bioink
papers.abstract: A novel bioink and a dispensing technique for 3D tissue-engineering applications are presented. The technique incorporates a coaxial extrusion needle using a low-viscosity cell-laden bioink to produce highly defined 3D biostructures. The extrusion system is then coupled to a microfluidic device to control the bioink arrangement deposition, demonstrating the versatility of the bioprinting technique. This low-viscosity cell-responsive bioink promotes cell migration and alignment within each fiber organizing the encapsulated cells. As a service to our authors and readers, this journal provides supporting information supplied by the authors. Such materials are peer reviewed and may be re-organized for online delivery, but are not copy-edited or typeset. Technical support issues arising from supporting information (other than missing files) should be addressed to the authors. Please note: The publisher is not responsible for the content or functionality of any supporting information supplied by the authors. Any queries (other than missing content) should be directed to the corresponding author for the article.

llm.relevance_to_user: 不涉及人工智能，仅聚焦于微流控生物打印硬件和生物墨水开发。
llm.why_not_core: No AI/ML method is used; focuses solely on microfluidic bioprinting hardware and bioink formulation, lacking algorithm integration, data-driven optimization, or autonomous decision-making.

summary_zh.motivation: 开发低粘度生物墨水并实现异质性组织构建
summary_zh.method: 使用同轴挤出针头耦合微流控装置进行生物打印
summary_zh.result: 成功打印高度有序的3D生物结构并促进细胞迁移排列
summary_zh.validation: 通过细胞培养观察验证生物墨水支持细胞活性

summary_en.motivation: Develop a low-viscosity bioink and dispensing technique for heterogeneous 3D tissue constructs.
summary_en.method: Coupled coaxial extrusion needle with a microfluidic device to control bioink deposition.
summary_en.result: Achieved highly defined 3D biostructures with cell migration and alignment within fibers.
summary_en.validation: Cell viability and migration were validated in vitro.

papers.title: The Relationship Between Cobalt/Chromium Ratios and the High Prevalence of Head-Stem Junction Corrosion in Metal-on-Metal Total Hip Arthroplasty
papers.first_author_affiliation: Institute of Orthopaedics and Musculoskeletal Science, University College London, Royal National Orthopaedic Hospital, Stanmore, United Kingdom

corresponding_authors.name: Harry Hothi
corresponding_authors.affiliation: Institute of Orthopaedics and Musculoskeletal Science, University College London, Royal National Orthopaedic Hospital, Stanmore, United Kingdom

llm.relevance_to_user: 与髋关节植入物应力遮挡和微动分析无关，仅涉及金属离子腐蚀临床问题。
llm.why_not_core: No quantification of proximal femur stress, micromotion, or any FEA/mechanical modeling; purely clinical corrosion study with no biomechanical analysis.

summary_zh.motivation: 探究金属对金属全髋关节置换中钴铬比与头颈连接处腐蚀的关系。
summary_zh.method: 回顾性临床研究，测量患者血清金属离子浓度。
summary_zh.result: 发现高比例的腐蚀病例，钴铬比值升高与腐蚀相关。

summary_en.motivation: To investigate the correlation between cobalt-to-chromium ratios and head-stem junction corrosion in metal-on-metal total hip arthroplasty.
summary_en.method: A retrospective clinical study measuring serum metal ion levels in patients with metal-on-metal hip implants.
summary_en.result: A high prevalence of head-stem corrosion was found, with elevated cobalt/chromium ratios significantly associated with corrosion.
summary_en.validation: Clinical serum metal ion data from a patient cohort.
